## Key Drivers

• **RBI bond sales tightened banking-system liquidity** — The RBI’s plan to drain ₹1 trillion via bond sales was a major liquidity tightening expected to push yields higher. This pressured rate-sensitive bank holdings including ICICI Bank, State Bank of India, Axis Bank, and Kotak Mahindra Bank, which are significant fund positions. ICICI Bank also extended a multi-session losing streak, and SBI weakened after the announcement.

• **Rising FCNR(B) deposit hedging costs added margin pressure** — Higher hedging costs on FCNR(B) deposits can squeeze net interest margins at banks. This weighed on ICICI Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank in particular, compounding the sector’s broader liquidity and rate concerns.

• **Company-specific bank negatives added to the drag** — Axis Bank faced regulatory uncertainty from consultations on charging fees for large UPI transactions, while Kotak Mahindra Bank saw the resignation of a Group President. Both developments weighed on those holdings alongside the broader banking-sector pressure.

• **Maruti Suzuki flagged a festive-season vehicle shortage** — Production constraints and vehicle shortage ahead of the festive season, with supplies not improving until January 2027, were a direct negative for near-term sales. This weighed on Maruti Suzuki, a fund holding in the auto sector.

• **HDFC Bank provided a partial offset** — HDFC Bank rose as CEO candidates were submitted to the RBI and brokerage views turned constructive, including a Jefferies note suggesting foreign investors may reallocate toward Indian financials. This was the main explained positive counterweight to the week’s banking weakness.

## Overall Summary

The fund ended the week lower, primarily because its large banking exposure was hit by the RBI’s liquidity-draining bond sales and by rising FCNR(B) deposit costs that threaten bank margins. Additional company-specific negatives at Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank, plus a festive-season vehicle shortage at Maruti Suzuki, added to the drag. HDFC Bank’s gain on CEO-process optimism and supportive brokerage views provided a meaningful partial offset. The takeaway is that financial-sector rate and liquidity headwinds drove the week’s performance, with HDFC Bank softening but not reversing the decline.
